diagram_previews.alt: The unit circle with points A, B and C, the triangle ABC in grey and the red circle on diameter AB; the radii OA and OB form an angle greater than 90 degrees, and O lies inside the red circle.
The unit circle with A, B and C all on a blue quarter-circle arc; the three red circles on AB, BC and CA as diameters are small and all lie away from the centre O.

difficulty_rationale: Two connected insights are needed: the origin is inside the circle on AB exactly when angle AOB is obtuse, and the complement is that all three points lie on a quarter circle, whose probability needs a careful disjoint-events count.
